Redesign drawback: the readme is now narrow and can't expand, so <pre> text shows scrollbars, and headings have little whitespace, which looks cramped.
There is no way to browse or search projects hosted on Bitbucket, for example by language. The main page only shows screenshots and signup links. Wants an 'Explore' feature like GitHub's.

Chose self-hosted GitLab over Bitbucket or GitHub because it already has most of these features and allows multiple private repos on a cheap VPS. Sees no innovation in the redesign that puts Bitbucket ahead.
Likes the 'Approve' button on commits for peer review, something GitHub lacks.

Likes Bitbucket's issue management much more than GitHub's. Hosting on Bitbucket plus free HipChat for small teams makes managing projects entirely through Atlassian fantastic.

A disaster for me: I've got dozens of hg repos on Bitbucket. Without automated conversion, there's probably no reason to keep using Bitbucket.
Shocked that all Mercurial repos will be deleted on June 1, 2020 rather than archived read-only like Google Code and CodePlex did. Historically interesting repos will disappear.

Daily Bitbucket user: navigation hasn't improved. Browsing source code on the web is painful, and quickly looking through someone's repository takes a lot of clicking and is way too slow compared to GitHub's tree slider UI.
After importing some repos and poking around, 'you really get what you pay for.' GitHub completely trounces Bitbucket on ease of use and toolset.
None of my existing Bitbucket repos have a Git link, and I can't find a way to add Git support from the Admin screen. Git is only offered as an option when creating a new repo.

Cancelling my $7 GitHub account and paying Bitbucket $10/month even with only 2 users. I'd rather pay for storage/users than per repo, since I have too many small private repos to keep paying GitHub for.

Switching markup from Creole to Markdown is very good news, and the preview is back in issue comments, though I'd prefer a live preview. The readme taking center stage on the overview page is nice, but it oddly appears again on the source page.
The redesigned commits view is 100 times better than GitHub's ever was. It shows much more info, including a graph like in gitx.

Redesign drawback: the readme is now narrow and can't expand, so <pre> text is too wide and shows scrollbars. There's also little whitespace around headings, so it looks cramped. Still nicer on the whole.
There's no way to browse or search projects hosted on Bitbucket, e.g. by language. The main page only shows screenshots and signup links. It needs an 'Explore' feature like GitHub's.

I prefer Mercurial, and Bitbucket offers unlimited private repos, so I only use GitHub for OSS and Bitbucket for everything else. I always recommend it to friends and companies looking for hosted repos.
I stopped paying $12/month for GitHub and moved all my private repositories to Bitbucket. Since it's just me working on them, it's totally free.
Their support is great. They bailed us out of a nasty mess we got tangled up in with our repo.

Recently started using Bitbucket and really like it, but the team feature is difficult to understand and not very intuitive. SVN support seems to be gone, so I'll have to re-import old repos using Git.
I use Bitbucket at work. And it stinks compared to GitHub.
For small teams, hosting on Bitbucket with free HipChat and managing projects through Atlassian is fantastic. I also like Bitbucket's issue management more than GitHub's.
Bitbucket's deploy keys fit typical use better than GitHub's. They are read-only and one key can be attached to multiple repos, whereas GitHub's are read-write and limited to a single repo.

Per-user pricing makes Bitbucket much more cost effective in an agency environment with a repo per client or per project. GitHub's per-repo pricing suits product businesses with only a handful of repos.
I chose Bitbucket over GitHub specifically because of Mercurial support. Dropping it is a damn shame.
I've used Bitbucket with Mercurial since 2011 and have more than 50 hg repos I'll need to move manually. They need to provide at least a single-click convert-to-git option.

In Bitbucket enterprise cloud there appears to be no way for an admin to prevent team members from making repositories public. Since we handle sensitive data, I may look at on-prem options or GitHub enterprise cloud for better permissions.

Shocked that all Mercurial repositories will be removed rather than archived read-only like Google Code and CodePlex did. Historically interesting repos will disappear if owners aren't monitoring their email.
